Free quick tunnel = for TESTING only
• random name — changes on every restart
  (your friends' links stop working)
• no uptime guarantee
• max 200 requests at once (more → error)
• no live push updates (SSE)
• no bandwidth / time cap published

Free DuckDNS = volunteer-run
• no uptime guarantee (runs on donations)
• only yourname.duckdns.org — no own domain
• 1 TXT record at a time (certificates are
  issued one name per step)
• ~5 names per account (reported)
• IPv6: your server must send it (no auto-detect)

Free Tailscale Funnel = at a company
• needs a Tailscale account (Google/GitHub/… login)
• address: selfprivacy.<tailnet>.ts.net
  (no own domain)
• switch Funnel on once, in your browser
• ONE name only → the app's API, not the
  cloud. / git. / matrix. / meet. services
• bandwidth limits (not published) · still beta
• a new name can take ~10 min to work
• the relay passes your traffic on but can't
  read it (the encryption ends on your server)

Keeping the same address
• the key is used once; after that the
  server proves who it is with its own
  ID file on its disk (tailscaled.state)
• reboot / new home ip: same machine,
  same address — but today the tunnel
  only comes back when you re-run the
  finish step
• reinstall wipes the ID file → a new
  machine selfprivacy-1, old links stop
  working: delete the old machine first
  (fix planned: keep the ID file)
• its login runs out after 180 days:
  switch off key expiry on Tailscale's
  Machines page

steps.caption: First you make a Tailscale account and get a one-time auth key from Tailscale.
steps.label: account
steps.title: Make a Tailscale account

steps.caption: You give the one-time auth key you got from Tailscale to your SelfPrivacy server. That machine registers itself at Tailscale, where it gets a domain name.
steps.label: install
steps.title: Install, then register at Tailscale

steps.caption: Tailscale keeps its own DNS phonebook. Its helper takes your domain name and Tailscale's relay address from the shelf and writes them in, so others can find your server (through the relay).
steps.label: phonebook
steps.title: Tailscale writes the name in its phonebook

steps.caption: The server keeps its own key (its ID file). You keep a copy, locked in KeePass on your computer, so a reinstall can come back as the same machine (planned: round0 R2). The Tailscale address comes along too.
steps.label: backup
steps.title: Keep a copy of the server's own key

steps.caption: You send your Tailscale address to a friend, for example in a chat message.
steps.label: share
steps.title: Send your friend the link

steps.caption: Your friend opens the Tailscale address. In the background the DNS phonebook turns the name your friend typed into an address, and the connection comes through the relay to your SelfPrivacy server.
steps.label: friend
steps.title: A friend opens the link
